[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/06/03 (Sat) 07:50

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a draft for the "Critique of the Loan Structure" section of the memo.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The proposed loan structure represents a shift away from traditional grant funding sources.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Revenue-backed loans offer an attractive alternative for covering part or all of the costs.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The borrower is the community water board, which may pose a challenge in terms of their ability to repay the loan.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Community water boards in developing countries often lack the resources and expertise needed to manage a loan effectively.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Default would result in financial losses for both parties.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The loan is secured by the assignment and pledge of net revenues of the water system.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The borrower must covenant in the loan agreement that tariffs will be set so that annual net revenues are equal to 120% of annual debt service.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] This could lead to a situation where the borrower must increase tariffs to unsustainable levels.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Any net revenues left after payment of interest and principal on the loan will be placed in a maintenance reserve fund.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Periodic and auditable financial reports are required to be prepared by the borrower.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The potential risks associated with the borrower's ability to repay the loan and generate sufficient revenue while maintaining affordable tariffs should be taken into account.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The long-term sustainability of the water system should also be carefully considered.

[USER] Requested to edit the Critique of the Loan Structure to include a hypothetical case study in Honduras.

- [FACT] Monthly Household Bill: Monthly O&M $1,041.67, Monthly Debt Service $5,774.31, Number of households paying 237.5, Monthly bill $28.70.
- [FACT] For every $10,000 grant, it takes down the monthly bill by $0.70.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant reiterated that the loan structure may have limitations and risks that need to be carefully considered.
